faq.question: Where is the best craft beer in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Strange Brewing in Colegiales is Reddit’s unanimous #1 for hop-forward beers. Desarmadero Bar in Palermo has 41 taps featuring the country’s best craft producers. On Tap in Palermo Hollywood has 20+ Argentine craft beers on draft.

faq.question: How much does craft beer cost in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Craft beer costs 1,500–5,000 ARS per pint ($1.50–$5 USD). Budget spots like The Prancing Pony charge 1,000 ARS. A full night costs what 1-2 pints would in London or NYC.

faq.question: What are the best craft beer neighborhoods in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Palermo is the epicenter with Desarmadero, On Tap, Growlers, and Rabieta. San Telmo has Bierlife and Antares. Colegiales has Strange Brewing (#1 pick). Recoleta has pioneering Buller Brewing. Off-the-beaten-path: Boedo (Prancing Pony) and Devoto (Geppetto).

faq.question: What Argentine craft beer brands should I try?
faq.answer: Strange Brewing (world-class IPAs), Juguetes Perdidos (innovative), Prinston (solid across styles), Sir Hopper (hop-focused), Astor (reliable), Minga (Patagonia-based). Find most at multi-tap bars like Desarmadero and Geppetto.

faq.question: Can I do a craft beer tour in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Yes — guided tours cover 3-4 breweries in Palermo or San Telmo. Self-guide: start at Desarmadero in Palermo, walk to Growlers, cab to Strange Brewing. For San Telmo: Bierlife then Antares in the Mercado.

faq.question: Is Buenos Aires good for craft beer?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Buenos Aires transformed from Quilmes-only to one of South America’s best craft beer cities. Quality IPAs compete with US craft breweries at a fraction of the price.

methodology: We analyzed 80+ Reddit posts and 300+ comments across r/BuenosAires, r/CraftBeer, r/beer, and r/ArgentinaTravel — spanning 2020 to 2026. Bars were cross-referenced with Google Maps ratings (minimum 4.0★), craft beer travel blogs, and TripAdvisor. We weighted responses from BA residents and repeat craft beer travelers more heavily than tourist one-offs.
